<details>
This is a routine, well-formed PKGBUILD for a prebuilt binary package. The `source_x86_64`/`source_aarch64` arrays fetch the release tarball from the package's own official upstream (github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code) and a LICENSE file from the same upstream organization, both with pinned, concrete sha256 checksums. There are no `SKIP` checksums, no VCS sources, and no build-time fetching or execution of unchecked content.

The `package()` function performs only standard installation steps: copying the provided `kimi` executable to `/usr/bin/kimi` and installing the LICENSE under `/usr/share/licenses`. There is no use of `eval`, `base64`, `curl | bash`, obfuscated code, dynamic code execution, file-exfiltration logic, or modification of anything outside the package's own install scope. The comments about glibc/gcc-libs dependencies and the `conflicts` declarations are normal packaging metadata for a Bun-compiled Node CLI that shares a binary name with older packages. Nothing here deviates from standard AUR packaging practice, and no genuinely malicious behavior is present.
</details>
